concepts.credibleEnvelope: None as an all-weather solo follow-cam (avail fails). In simulation, with the nominal polar and mass and IF a ≤3 mm boom could launch/dock the KCU, it would deliver ≈83 % in head/cross winds 3–9 m/s on low-traffic pistes with written permission; calm 78 %, tailwinds 24–69 %. The boom premise fails a closed-form check, so even that envelope is not credible until the dock/boom is redesigned and re-run.
concepts.auditVerdict: Reproduces the 48-case ensemble (avail 72.25 % own vs 72.30 claimed; other metrics exact or within 0.1). Honest fail on avail; KE passes by 0.62 J and fails at L/D 0.6 / +15 % mass (reproduced 17.26 / 16.95 J). The new passive 3 mm boom does project <2 px (median 1.66 px) but cannot nest as a 6-section telescope, cannot hold the 90 g KCU in EXTEND/STOW and buckles at ≈1.3 N when hauling it in; a boom that can (≥5.7–8.7 mm) collapses avail to ≈6 %. The reel-motor envelope is real and respected. Clothesline unsolved. Not usable; research concept only.

EU: 124 g (<250 g) can be C0-class; C0 follow-me must stay ≤50 m from the remote pilot (2019/945 Part 1) — breached once (69.8 m) in the ensemble; A1 follow-me height ≤50 m.
US: Part 107/recreational rules require VLOS by the operator or a visual observer; a skier facing downhill cannot watch a glider behind them — no legal US solo operation without a waiver.
Resort written permission (gate for every concept); many resorts ban drones outright.
Landing at the lift approach (the most crowded spot) every run; no bystander detection in the landing logic beyond the rider.
Pusher prop near the hand at throw; snow strikes at 6–12 J.

consistencyChecks.finding: windEstimate() seeds its ±1 m/s bias from the case seed, so the 48-case grid samples only 3 bias draws per wind. leapfrog keMax and C0 range pass on seeds 11–13 but fail on seeds 14–22 (tail5.5_s15 15.03 J / 54.9 m; tail6_s17 16.05 J; tail5.5_s20 15.49 J; tail6_s21 50.5 m). towglider passes all 48 but crossL7.5_s11 (off-grid, gate on) gives headClear 0.934 m. kite2 KE margin 0.62 J. Grid-only safety maxima are not robust.

consistencyChecks.metric: idealised estimators still in judged runs (rule 5)
consistencyChecks.finding: All launch/park gates use windEstimate() (compliant for all three). But: leapfrog tracker latency compensation and GNSS feed-forward use the true LOS increment/rate (+noise, 50 Hz) and guidance uses true rider state; towglider camera mount is pointed from the true rider position; kite2 window controller uses noise-free kite position/velocity and true dynamic pressure. Effects measured: leapfrog jitter 1.64 → 2.01 (est. comp, 5 Hz GNSS) → 3.43 (1 Hz GNSS, avail 64.6 %); towglider 2.45 → 2.56–2.81 with 3–5 % detection noise; kite2 doubled noise avail +1 pp, KE 14.31 J.
consistencyChecks.favours: leapfrog (jitter/avail rest on the rider-tag link rate)

consistencyChecks.finding: Shared artefactCounts(≥2 px) is applied, but each concept projects its own parts. towglider tests the leash only at polyline vertices (misses the near-camera segment 3–13 px) and omits the 3 mm wand (−1.4 pp own test, −6.7 pp if the subject box includes skis). kite2 boom 1.66 px median meets the rule only because it is 3 mm (structurally infeasible, A4-K2-01). "Bounding box" of the subject is not defined (body vs incl. skis).

consistencyChecks.metric: worn rigid members excluded from headClear
consistencyChecks.finding: kite2 passive boom (free pivot, moves with the line) 0.33 m from the helmet centre; towglider wand 1.165 m (included would pass). Exclusion of a free-pivoting boom as "worn rigid" is generous; with a buildable 1.2 m boom kite2 headClear 0.84 m.

leapfrog sensitivity figures relayed in the round-4 report (mass +10 % → 69.7 %, bias ±2 → 17.65 J, stow 13.5 s → 33.1 s) are not in dev/leapfrog/results.json (18-case subset: 65.6 %, 17.92 J, 33.4 s); auditor full-48: 67.7 %, 17.92 J, 33.2 s. Same direction, all fail.

ranking.question: usable solo follow-cam (self-operated, full run, real winds, minimal set-up) — round 4

usableInSimulation.leapfrog: conditionally yes, only inside a light-tailwind envelope: groomed low-traffic piste, calm/cross/head ≤9 m/s, true tailwind ≤≈5 m/s with the launch gate tightened to ≈5 m/s estimated, rider downhill speed ≤≈11 m/s, airframe ≤≈172 g, feathered wing CLmax ≥1.2, rider tag GNSS ≥5 Hz. Not for all-weather use (seeds 14–22 tail 5.5–6 m/s exceed 14.9 J / 50 m).
usableInSimulation.kite2: no — fails avail (72.3 %), and the passive 3 mm boom that makes the artefact rule pass is structurally infeasible (cannot cantilever/compress the KCU); a buildable 6→5 mm boom gives avail ≈6 %.
usableInSimulation.towglider: no — fails avail (48–49 %; launched runs 74 % mean so 80 % is unreachable); light-wind research concept only.

ranking.summary: leapfrog is the only concept passing all 13 judged metrics as modelled (5 conditional) and reproduces exactly, but its avail margin is 2.3 pp and its KE/C0-range margins fail on unseen seeds in the 5.5–6 m/s tail band. kite2 and towglider honestly fail avail. Ranking is by credible usable envelope × evidence × safety, not by count of passes. Evidence: numerical uncalibrated simulation; nothing physically tested.

order.label: only all-13 pass as modelled; thin, light-tailwind envelope
order.rationale: Exact reproduction; avail 82.46 (2.3 pp margin; lost at mass +8–10 % or CLmax 1.1), jitter 1.64 (2.01 with estimated tracker comp at 5 Hz GNSS, 3.43 fail at 1 Hz), setup p90 24.7 s (stow 13.5 s → 33 s fail), ops p90 2 (max 3), KE 13.75 J and headClear 2.01 m on grid; seeds 14–22 tail 5.5–6 → KE up to 16.05 J and 54.9 m range. Morphing wing goes beyond Ajanic 2020 (+100 % area by sliding feathers vs +41 % by sweep, CLmax 1.25 at Re≈34k, one 2.5 g servo). No tether/clothesline hazard. Needs a tighter tail gate (≈5 m/s est.) — not yet re-judged for avail.

order.label: fails avail; boom premise infeasible; clothesline unfixed
order.rationale: Reproduces (avail 72.25 vs 72.30, KE 14.275); winch now within a real 2205/25 A envelope (A3-K2-04 fixed). But the passive 3 mm, 1.45 m boom that meets the 2 px rule cannot nest 6 sections or carry/dock the 90 g KCU (≈930 MPa root stress, buckles at ≈1.3–2 N); a buildable 6→5 mm boom → avail ≈6 %. KE margin 0.62 J (L/D 0.6 → 17.26 J, mass +15 % → 16.95 J). Line 0.74–0.84 m above snow 1–3 m behind in every run. Strongest wind robustness of the flown concepts (non-tail 83 %), hence rank 2.

order.label: lowest burden, safe on grid by refusing, fails avail structurally
order.rationale: Exact reproduction; ops 1, setup 12 s, 0.46 kg, KE 13.2 J. avail 48.0 (17/48 refused; launched 74 % mean so ≥80 % unreachable; pre-run history → 53 %). Tail-band hazard of round 3 fixed by refusing ≥3.5 m/s. crossL7.5_s11 headClear 0.934 m off-grid. Jitter pass needs ≥6 Hz loaded servo (4 Hz → 4.4 °/s fail); endurance needs a 0.05 W lift sleep (0.5 W → 40 min fail).

order.label: frozen negative result (round-2 row unchanged)
order.rationale: Round-2 audit: fails avail 29.6 %, setup 60 s, ops p90 3, KE 18 J, jitter p90 18 °/s. Not re-run.
